newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian govt may introduce draft tax laws to Duma.
newsitem.headline: Russian govt may introduce draft tax laws to Duma.

text.p: The Russian government may try to implement key parts of its new tax code, currently bogged down in the State Duma lower house of parliament, by introducing separate laws on the main issues, a government spokesman said on Tuesday.

"Work on the new tax code is going on with much difficulty and if it becomes clear that approval will take much time, I cannot rule out the possibility that the government will think it expedient to introduce several draft laws which reflect the main ideas of the tax code to the Duma," Igor Shabdurasulov told a news conference.
The government sent the second, third and fourth parts of the draft tax code to the Duma last month. The first part was submitted last year.
The tax code envisages reduction of a number of taxes and the total tax burden on companies, and the government sees it as a key to econmic revival.
The International Monetary Fund, which is backing Russian reforms with a $10 billion credit, had insisted the government submit the tax code to the Duma before it would disburse any money this year.
The government says the 1998 budget will be based on the new code.
